rv.q: Church Hurt is a vital and compassionate portrait of how those roots nurture and strangle at the same time.
The conversations between them all are laugh out loud funny and often a thoughtful exploration of how to exist in a world where the definition of what is an acceptable identity is extremely narrow.
Their journeys, both separately and collectively, are thrilling to watch and hear.
Keep an eye on this company; I feel they are one to reckon with.

cn.t: Critics praise this world premiere for its thoughtful exploration of faith, trauma, and redemption within a megachurch setting, with Brynne Frauenhoffer's storytelling drawing acclaim for venturing into rarely explored emotional territory.
